output.summary: A perennial herb native to western, central and northern Europe, it forms ground-hugging rosettes and readily colonises lawns despite mowing. Its white, often red-tipped flower heads close at night, open in the morning and follow the sun.
output.edibilityNote: Young leaves are eaten raw or cooked; older leaves become more astringent. Flower buds and petals are eaten raw, and the plant is used as tea.
